title: MJ: Multi-turn LLM Jailbreaking via Decomposed Credit Assignment
claim: A two-phase training loop generates multi-turn rollouts, then converts turn-level rewards into decomposed credit for policy updates.
layout: 2 stacked phase panels, left-to-right then loops back, math boxes
description: A two-band diagram. The top band, Phase 1 Multi-Turn Rollout Generation, flows left to right: an Attacker skull icon sends a harmful behavior x0 into the Attacker Policy box (a target icon, with a flame marking it as trainable). That box emits an adversarial prompt x_{i,t} to a frozen Victim Model (snowflake, brain icon), whose response y_{i,t} goes to a frozen Judge Model (scales icon). The judge outputs a turn-level reward r_{i,t} (+0.9). Small quote boxes show example text. The bottom band, Phase 2 DC-GRPO Optimization, runs right to left. A grid of G×T rollout data triples (x, y, r) feeds a green Decomposed Credit Assignment box. That box stacks immediate credit and future credit into the DC-GRPO advantage formula. The advantage passes to a GRPO Update box, and a bold arrow returns to the attacker policy.
caption: Multi-turn RL training loop. Given a harmful behavior x0, the attacker πθ generates prompts xi,t and the victim πvictim responds with yi,t across T turns per group. The judge scores each turn, producing ri,t. All G rollouts with T turns are collected before the parameter update. GRPO then computes group-relative advantages and updates θ in a single step.
abstract: Modern large language models (LLMs) operate in interactive multi-turn settings, making multi-turn jailbreaking a realistic threat model and an important setting for automated red teaming. A core challenge in learning multi-turn jailbreak attackers is credit assignment: different turns contribute differently to the final outcome, yet existing learning signals are often too coarse to identify their individual contributions. We propose decomposed credit GRPO (DC-GRPO), a unified turn-level credit assignment framework for Group Relative Policy Optimization in multi-turn jailbreak learning. DC-GRPO assigns a separate group-relative learning signal to each turn by combining immediate and future credit, avoiding the credit misassignment induced by broadcasting a single trajectory-level score across the dialogue. We instantiate this framework with static and dynamic weighting rules that differ in how the two credit sources are balanced while sharing the same turn-level structure. Across four victim LLMs and three benchmarks, DC-GRPO achieves up to 98.26% average ASR_5@3, substantially outperforming the state-of-the-art methods, including SEMA (86.58%) and TROJail (86.23%), demonstrating the effectiveness of our turn-level group-relative credit assignment. Warning: This paper contains examples of harmful content.
